newsitem.title: NORWAY: Israeli foreign minister sees deal on Hebron soon.
newsitem.headline: Israeli foreign minister sees deal on Hebron soon.

text.p: Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy said on Tuesday Israel remained committed to a deal with Palestinian authorities over the West Bank town of Hebron and he believed agreement would be reached soon.

Levy, on a two-day official visit to the Norwegian capital, said two points continued to block the long-overdue agreement on troop redeployment in Hebron, where 400 Jewish settlers live among 100,000 Palestinians.
"Security is at the centre of these issues," Levy said after talks with his Norwegian counterpart Bjoern Tore Godal.

"I believe these two issues can be resolved in a meeting between the (Israeli) Prime Minister and Chairman (Yasser) Arafat...If there is willingness on both sides there should be no difficulty and I can assure you there is willingness on the Israeli side."
Israeli-Palestinian negotiations have been locked in stalemate since the government of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu took over office in June.
Netanyahu wants to modify security arrangements agreed in a partial pullout deal agreed by the Palestinian Liberation Organisation (PLO) and the former Israeli Labour government in September 1993.
Israel is insisting its troops be allowed to enter parts of the city under PLO control when in pursuit of suspected guerrillas.
"We have the intention of implementing the agreement on Hebron. Some very important issues, concerning security, are included in the original agreement and they are vital to us," Levy told reporters.

"Dragging on this issue does not serve any purpose. A vacuum created in this way is not part of the agreement, you don't advance in a vacuum. Therefore I hope these few issues can be resolved quickly and we will be able to move on in the process."
Godal said Norway, encouraged by signs that Israel and the PLO were nearing a deal, would leave its observer force in place in Hebron.
Norway has around 40 monitors in the sensitive area, the only international force there, and has previously said it would not renew the mandate for them if a deal is not struck soon.
"We have stated many times that we cannot stay there for eternity. But as long as there is real development in the negotiations we are not the ones to make major difficutlties," Godal said.

Levy, whose visit coincided with a World Jewish Congress conference on the restitution of Jewish property confiscated during the Holocaust, said Israel's expansion of settlement areas in the West Bank and Gaza Strip -- another contentious area in the peace process -- was proceeding cautiously.
The PLO has blasted Israel for approving the construction of thousands of new homes in the settlements, where more than 130,000 Jews live amid nearly two million Palestinians .

"This government is proceeding with a lot of caution because the main issue is to continue with the peace process. There was no decision by this government to create new settlements and as far as answering the needs of existing settlements this government is not doing anymore than the former Labour Party government did in the past," he said.
